subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: The induction of a potential difference in a conductor when it moves relative to a magnetic field
The heating of a wire when a current passes through it
The force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field
The storage of charge on two parallel plates
questions.explain: The generator effect is the induction of a potential difference (and a current if the circuit is complete) when a conductor and magnetic field move relative to one another.

questions.q: For a potential difference to be induced in a straight wire, the wire must:
options: Be held stationary in a strong field
questions.explain: A pd is induced only when the conductor cuts (crosses) magnetic field lines, so relative movement between conductor and field is required.

questions.q: Which change would increase the size of the induced potential difference in a generator?
options: Reducing the number of turns on the coil
questions.explain: Increasing the speed of movement, the field strength or the number of turns all increase the induced pd.

questions.q: A magnet is pushed into a coil, inducing a current in one direction. What happens when the magnet is then pulled out?
options: The current is induced in the opposite direction
The current stays in the same direction
No current is induced at all
The current doubles in the same direction
questions.explain: Reversing the direction of relative movement reverses the direction of the induced current.

questions.q: Why is no potential difference induced when a magnet is held still inside a coil?
options: No magnetic field lines are being cut
The coil has too much resistance
questions.explain: Without relative movement the conductor cuts no field lines, so no pd is induced.

questions.q: What type of current does an alternator produce?
questions.explain: An alternator uses slip rings so it produces alternating current.

questions.q: Which component allows a dynamo to produce direct current rather than alternating current?
questions.explain: A dynamo uses a split-ring commutator to reverse the connections each half-turn, giving a direct current.

questions.q: How does the output of an alternator appear on a potential difference against time graph?
options: A curve that alternates between positive and negative values
A curve that stays positive at all times
questions.explain: An alternator's a.c. output oscillates smoothly between positive and negative pd as the coil rotates.

questions.q: A generator coil rotates 50 times every second. What is the frequency of the a.c. output?
questions.explain: Frequency in hertz equals the number of complete rotations per second, so 50 rotations per second gives 50 Hz.

questions.q: Transformers only work with which type of supply?
questions.explain: Transformers need a continually changing magnetic field, which only alternating current provides.

questions.q: A transformer has more turns on its secondary coil than on its primary coil. This is a:
options: Step-up transformer that increases the potential difference
Step-down transformer that decreases the potential difference
Transformer that has no effect on potential difference
Device that converts a.c. into d.c.
questions.explain: When the secondary has more turns than the primary the output pd is greater, so it is a step-up transformer.

questions.q: Why must a transformer be supplied with alternating current to work?
options: It produces a continually changing magnetic field that induces a pd in the secondary coil
It keeps the iron core permanently magnetised
It prevents the core from overheating
It stops the primary coil from rusting
questions.explain: Alternating current creates a constantly changing magnetic field in the core, which induces an alternating pd in the secondary coil.

questions.q: Which equation correctly relates the potential differences and turns of a transformer?
questions.explain: The transformer equation states that the ratio of primary to secondary pd equals the ratio of primary to secondary turns.

questions.q: A transformer has 100 turns on the primary coil and 400 turns on the secondary. If the primary pd is 20 V, what is the secondary pd?
A step-down transformer reduces 240 V to 12 V. If the primary coil has 2000 turns, how many turns are on the secondary coil?
In the National Grid, what does a step-up transformer do before electricity is transmitted through the cables?
options: Increases the potential difference and decreases the current
Decreases the potential difference and increases the current
Converts alternating current into direct current
Increases both the potential difference and the current
questions.explain: Step-up transformers raise the pd and lower the current for efficient transmission across the grid.

questions.q: Why is electricity transmitted through the National Grid at a very high potential difference?
options: A lower current reduces energy wasted as heat in the cables
A higher current makes the cables cheaper
It converts the supply to direct current
questions.explain: High pd means low current, and since power loss depends on the square of the current, less energy is wasted heating the transmission cables.

questions.q: An ideal (100% efficient) transformer has a primary power input of 500 W. If the secondary pd is 250 V, what is the current in the secondary coil?
questions.explain: For a 100% efficient transformer power out equals power in, so I = P/V = 500/250 = 2 A.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Physics (1PH0) specification; Electromagnetic Induction
